chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! I fear the scorpions.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look at the Daughters of Na'sh (Ursa Minor), the three stars; the middle one of them, by its side is a small star near it, which the Arabs call As-Suha, and we call it Aslam. Gaze at it with a solitary gaze every night, and say three times:'
O Allah! Lord of Aslam! Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Hasten their relief and Keep us safe.
Is'haq said: 'So I did not neglect it since my time (of having learnt that) except for once, so the scorpion stung me.'

key_terms.أَسْلَمَ: Aslam (The Shia name for the star Al-Suha)
key_terms.فَرَجَهُمْ: Their relief (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt or the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific dua and celestial sign for protection from scorpions in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribed a specific supplication involving gazing at the star Aslam (Al-Suha) in the constellation Ursa Minor to seek protection from scorpion stings. This practice highlights the Shia tradition of linking celestial signs with divine protection, where the star's name 'Aslam' (Submission) resonates with the concept of surrendering to God's will. The narration emphasizes the efficacy of this practice, noting that the narrator was stung only once when he neglected it, underscoring the importance of consistent dhikr.
